title: Voice Loom — priority weave of customer asks and micro-plays
body:
Purpose
---
Quick synthesis of customer feedback threads collected May–June 2026 (support tickets, 1:1 interviews, NPS replies, partner conversations). The goal: produce an execution-oriented map of 1) recurring friction points, 2) compact feature asks, and 3) concrete micro-plays (low-risk implementation steps) we can trial in the next 6–10 weeks. This is intentionally conversational — notes to self + handoff doc for product + eng.

Methodology
---
- Sources: 84 support threads tagged \"performance\", 23 customer interviews (mid-market & platform teams), 12 partner feedback packets, 6 NPS verbatims.
- Sorting heuristic: frequency x customer value x ease-of-probe (quick wins emphasized).
- Output: prioritized ask map, write-ups for three micro-plays, open questions for SRE/serving-runtime.

Topline themes (one-liners)
---
- Predictable latency wins: customers repeatedly ask for per-route SLO visibility and stronger fallbacks for heavy tails.
- Cost transparency: token-level billing still confusing for embedding-heavy workloads; request for per-caller and per-route spend breakdown.
- Private deployment ops friction: runtime config drift and onboarding scripts are painful for first on-prem pilot customers.
- Model variant assurances: customers want automated variant fallback + drift notifications rather than manual rollbacks.

Priority request map (ranked)
---
1) Per-route latency SLO dashboard + alerting (high impact, medium effort)
   - Asks: 95th/99th latency, token-level breakdown, per-model and per-route.
   - Rationale: reduces time-to-troubleshoot for product teams; repeatedly cited in 40% of performance threads.

2) Billing slice by route + caller (medium impact, low-medium effort)
   - Asks: UI + API to attribute token costs to routes and API keys; exportable CSV.
   - Rationale: customer finance teams need to reconcile costs; helps show value of caching/quantization.

3) Private deploy quickstart & drift-checker (high impact, medium-high effort)
   - Asks: opinionated terraform + Helm charts for a V1 on-prem pilot; a runtime health-check that detects config drift (kernel mismatch, quantization flags).
   - Rationale: accelerates enterprise on-prem adoption; repeatedly stalled pilots.

4) Auto-fallback policies for model variants (medium impact, medium effort)
   - Asks: opaque policy DSL in Console to specify fallback chains, and automatic rollbacks when regression metrics breach thresholds.
   - Rationale: reduces incidents during rollouts, improves reliability for apps sensitive to hallucination or latency spikes.

5) Cache isolation primitives for multi-tenant KV (low-medium impact, high effort)
   - Asks: per-tenant cache quotas and eviction policies; visibility into cache hit-rates per-tenant.

Micro-plays (concrete tests we can run quickly)
---
A) Latency Sprint: \"Route SLO Lite\" (3-week spike + experiment)
   - Deliverable: add 95th/99th latency lines to existing per-model dashboard for top 10 customer routes; add a lightweight alert (Slack + email) when route 99th exceeds baseline.
   - Success signal: demoed to 3 pilot customers; two show faster triage times on post-mortems.

B) Billing Export MVP (2-week scope)
   - Deliverable: CSV export mapped by API key and route for last 30 days, with token and estimated $ cost columns; a short help doc explaining quantization/embedding units.
   - Success signal: finance teams can reconcile within 48 hours; request volume for this feature drops in support queue.

C) Private Deploy Quickstart (6-week phased)
   - Phase 1 (2 weeks): opinionated repo with terraform + k8s manifests + sample smoke tests.
   - Phase 2 (4 weeks): add a basic drift-checker agent that compares deployed runtime kernels/configs to recommended baseline and surfaces mismatches in Console.
   - Success signal: first enterprise pilot spins up in <2 days and reports fewer initial infra blockers.

Conversation fragments and customer language (raw snippets)
---
- \"We love the throughput but when a route hits a tail it's impossible to tell if it's the model or our prompt.\"
- \"Our finance team asked for a single CSV to slice costs by product feature — otherwise we can't attribute value to the feature owners.\"
- \"Setting up private was doable but the little flags and defaults were the real time sink. If you had a one-click starter we'd sign up today.\"

Open questions (needs eng/product clarity)
---
- How feasible is adding per-route 99th latency without materially increasing metric ingestion costs? (SRE + Observability)
- Can we produce a reasonably accurate cost estimate per token for quantized models that customers trust? (Billing + Serving Runtime)
- What minimum set of checks should the drift-checker run for private deployments to be useful without being noisy? (Infra + Private Deployments)

Risks / guardrails
---
- Observability additions could increase cardinality and monitoring costs; start with top N routes and sample-based metrics.
- Billing exports risk confusion if not accompanied by a short explanation of token units and quantization effects; include a simple FAQ.
- Private deploy automation must not assume customer network/topology; provide opt-out and manual-check pathways.

Next steps / proposed owners
---
- Product: scope Latency Sprint + Billing Export MVP (owner: Sofia Alvarez) — due EoQ1 spike deliverables.
- Eng: sanity-check metric cost and plan sampling strategy (owner: Arjun Mehta).
- Infra: starter repo and drift-check design doc (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- CS: recruit 3 pilot customers for Route SLO Lite and Private Quickstart (owner: Riya Patel).

Appendix: quick impact/effort scoreboard (subjective)
---
- Route SLO dashboard: Impact high | Effort medium
- Billing export: Impact medium | Effort low
- Private quickstart + drift-checker: Impact high | Effort medium-high
- Auto-fallback policies: Impact medium | Effort medium
- Cache isolation: Impact low-medium | Effort high

Notes to self
---
- When sharing with product leadership: emphasize pilot feedback quotes and tie latency work to fewer incident hours for CS.
- Keep this doc live; update after pilot kickoffs.

End of notes.
